title: Culinary & Hospitality
tagline: From line cook to chef, from front desk to hotel leadership — the craft of feeding and hosting people.
summary: Restaurants, hotels, and beverage programs form one of the world's largest employers. This roadmap covers both sides of the house — kitchen craft (knife skills, stations, food cost) and guest service (bar, service flow, recovery) — plus the management, certifications, and ownership paths.

sources.label: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Hospitality spans kitchens (restaurants, hotels, catering, institutional) and guest-facing roles (service, bar, front office). Careers start fast, teach fast, and reward stamina and craft.
detail.why: It is one of the few industries where you can start earning this week, learn a genuine craft, and reach management or ownership without a degree.
learn: Read the BLS profile of chefs and head cooks
Tour two kitchens or hotels and note the role structure
Work one double shift as trial (many places allow stagiaire days)
Decide: back-of-house craft or front-of-house people work

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Kitchens run on a brigade (exec → sous → station chefs → prep/dish); front-of-house runs host → server/bartender → floor manager. Hotels add front desk, housekeeping leadership, and F&B management.
detail.why: Knowing the ladder helps you pick your entry point and see every promotion two steps ahead.
learn: Diagram a brigade line for a 60-seat restaurant
Identify the entry role that hires constantly in your city
Note which roles get tips vs salary in your market
Pick a two-year target role

resources.title: BLS OOH — Food and Serving Occupations

detail.description: Food safety is non-negotiable: temperature control, cross-contamination, allergens, handwashing, and sanitation cycles — codified in food-handler cards and ServSafe Manager certification.
detail.why: A food-handler card is a hiring requirement nearly everywhere; the manager-level ServSafe is required for anyone supervising a kitchen.
learn: Earn a food-handler card (local health department or ServSafe)
Learn the temperature danger zone and cooling rules
Master allergen protocols (the big 9 in the US)
Practice proper sanitizing solution use and test strips

certs.name: ServSafe Food Handler / Manager
certs.note: Food-handler card (entry) and manager certification (supervisory); widely required by health departments and employers.

detail.description: Great service is anticipatory: read the table, sequence the courses, know the menu cold, and recover failures gracefully. The mechanics are learnable; the warmth is a choice.
detail.why: Front-of-house earnings and promotion run on guest experience — and service instincts transfer to every people-facing career.
learn: Memorize a full menu with ingredients and modifications
Practice the table-visit rhythm (arrival, check-back, dessert, farewell)
Learn the recovery script: acknowledge, fix, gesture
Shadow the best server on staff for a shift

resources.title: BLS OOH — Food and Serving Occupations

detail.description: Kitchen craft starts with the knife: grip and cuts (dice, julienne, chiffonade), sharpening, and mise en place — everything prepped, labeled, and within reach before service.
detail.why: Speed and consistency in any kitchen come from clean knife work and obsessive mise; it is the first thing chefs judge.
learn: Practice the five mother cuts on 10 lbs of vegetables
Keep your knife sharp (learn whetstone sharpening)
Set up a full mise en place for a 3-dish prep list
Time yourself: consistency beats raw speed

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Line cooking is executing a station under pressure: firing tickets in order, holding quality at the rush, communicating ticket calls, and resetting fast.
detail.why: Line experience teaches composure, timing, and teamwork faster than any classroom — and it is the universal entry to kitchen careers.
learn: Master one station completely (sauté or grill)
Learn ticket reading and fire-order communication
Practice station breakdown and reset to standard
Work 20 services; note your error pattern and fix it
tasks: Prepare and cook food in a restaurant, ensuring quality and presentation standards are met.

detail.description: The canon: stocks, the five mother sauces, braising and roasting, seasoning layering, and butchery basics. Foundations are what make menus improvisable.
detail.why: Chefs promote cooks who understand why a sauce breaks or a braise toughens — foundations are the promotion currency.
learn: Make chicken and vegetable stock from scratch, correctly
Prepare all five mother sauces and two derivatives
Braise a tough cut to tenderness and explain the science
Break down a whole chicken into eight pieces

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: The pastry branch: precision baking, laminated doughs, plated desserts, chocolate, and breads — a distinct craft with its own ladder (pastry cook → pastry chef).
detail.why: Pastry suits precision-lovers and offers specialty careers in hotels, bakeries, and standalone shops.
learn: Learn baker's percentages and scale everything
Bake laminated dough (croissant) from scratch
Master one plated dessert with sauce work
Bake sandwich bread and lean hearth bread, compare crumb

detail.description: Prep is production cooking at scale: par levels, rotation (FIFO), labeling, and the receiving discipline that keeps the walk-in organized and costs down.
detail.why: Every chef started in prep; understanding inventory and waste here is the seed of kitchen management.
learn: Set par levels for one station for a week
Practice FIFO rotation and date labeling standards
Do a receiving check: quality, temperature, weights
Track one week of waste and propose two reductions

detail.description: Restaurants run on percentages: food cost (typically 28–35%), labor cost, and prime cost. Chefs who can cost a plate and engineer a menu become management immediately.
detail.why: Kitchen creativity survives only inside food-cost discipline — this is the skill that takes cooks to chef.
learn: Cost one recipe per ingredient and compute plate cost
Calculate food cost percentage from a sample P&L
Engineer a menu: stars, plow-horses, puzzles, dogs
Propose one spec change that saves 2% food cost

detail.description: Bartending blends craft (classics, balance, garnish), speed (service well), and responsibility (alcohol laws, checking IDs, refusing service). Coffee programs add their own craft ladder.
detail.why: Beverage roles pay well with tips and lead to bar management, beverage direction, and cafe ownership.
learn: Learn 10 classic cocktails cold (specs and technique)
Get your jurisdiction's alcohol-service certification (e.g., TIPS-style)
Practice free-pour accuracy and well organization
Learn espresso extraction basics if coffee-focused

detail.description: The operational backbone: POS fluency, reservation and waitlist management, table math (server sections, turns), and the closing-out cash discipline.
detail.why: Whoever runs the book and the POS quietly runs the floor — these are the promotion tasks nobody notices.
learn: Master your POS: voids, comps, splits, item 86-ing
Manage a Friday waitlist fairly and calmly
Learn server-banking cash reconciliation
Practice floor plans for three party-size mixes

resources.title: BLS OOH — Food and Serving Occupations

detail.description: Service failures are recoverable: acknowledge fast, fix without excuses, follow up with a gesture, and log patterns so the kitchen can prevent repeats.
detail.why: Recovered guests are often more loyal than never-disappointed ones — recovery skill is why managers get promoted from the floor.
learn: Write the three-step recovery script for your venue
Handle one complaint end-to-end this week
Track complaint patterns for a month
Practice empowering language ('here's what I can do…')

resources.title: BLS OOH — Food and Serving Occupations

detail.description: Sous and head chef work: scheduling the brigade, ordering, expediting, training, and enforcing standards — leadership delivered at 400 degrees.
detail.why: Kitchen management converts craft credibility into team results; it is the chef's real job description.
learn: Write a week's brigade schedule covering labor target
Run an expedite window calmly for full service
Train one cook on a station with a checklist
Run a prep list for a 200-cover night

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Reading the restaurant P&L: prime cost (food + labor, target ≤ 60–65%), rent, and the flow-through to profit. Managers who speak P&L get general-manager roles.
detail.why: General managers are hired to protect profit, not just pass inspections — the numbers are the language.
learn: Read a sample restaurant P&L line by line
Compute prime cost and flow-through on two months
Build a labor-scheduling target from forecast covers
Propose two profit actions with estimated impact

detail.description: Hotels run rooms division (front office, housekeeping) and F&B — with revenue management (rate and occupancy optimization) as the strategic brain. Lodging management is a distinct, global career.
detail.why: Hotel careers scale internationally with clear brand ladders — from front desk to rooms division to GM.
learn: Learn the front-office cycle: arrival, in-house, departure
Understand occupancy, ADR, and RevPAR metrics
Shadow a housekeeping inspector's morning
Read how F&B anchors hotel guest experience

detail.description: The chef ladder: sous chef → chef de cuisine → executive chef/culinary director — combining menu authorship, cost leadership, and brigade development, often across properties.
detail.why: Chef roles reward both craft and leadership; the path is open through proved kitchens or culinary school plus apprenticeship.
learn: Write a seasonal menu with costed recipes
Run kitchen interviews and try-outs
Develop two cooks deliberately (document their growth)
Stage at a kitchen you admire and take notes

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Opening a restaurant or cafe: concept and market fit, business plan, build-out and permits, menu engineering, staffing, and the survival math of the first year.
detail.why: Ownership is the dream and the hardest job in hospitality — going in with the numbers is the difference between dream and closure.
learn: Write a one-page concept: audience, price band, capacity
Model break-even covers per night
Learn permits and licensing in your city (health, liquor)
Interview two owners about their first year

detail.description: Culinary school (certificate to associate) buys structured foundations and network; apprenticeship/stagiaire paths buy paid experience. Most working chefs mix both.
detail.why: This is the field's biggest money decision — both routes work; debt without intent doesn't.
learn: Compare total cost of local programs vs earning while learning
Ask 5 working chefs which they'd choose today
Check if your target employers sponsor certifications
Consider community-college culinary programs for value

resources.title: BLS OOH — Chefs and Head Cooks

detail.description: Stackable credentials: ServSafe Manager (near-universal), alcohol-service cards, hotel-side credentials (e.g., AHLEI's lodging certifications), and sommelier/wine study for beverage careers.
detail.why: Certifications are cheap signal boosters in hiring and are often required for supervisory roles.
learn: Get ServSafe Manager if you supervise anything
Add your jurisdiction's alcohol-service card
Explore AHLEI lodging certifications for hotel tracks
Plan wine/beverage study only if beverage is your lane

certs.name: Certified Hotel Administrator (CHA)
certs.note: Hospitality executive credential for general managers and senior lodging leaders.

detail.description: Beyond restaurants: concierge and guest-relations roles, event and catering coordination, and destination-experience work — hospitality skills applied outside the dining room.
detail.why: Service craft is portable; these roles trade kitchen hours for business hours while keeping the people-first core.
learn: Learn the concierge role from O*NET
Explore catering and event operations (high-volume service)
Note local tourism employers (hotels, attractions)
Practice vendor coordination for one mock event

detail.description: The industry runs nights, weekends, holidays, on your feet, at pace. Sustainable careers plan for sleep, feet, hands, and honest pacing across a decade.
detail.why: Burnout, not skill, ends most hospitality careers — planning the physical reality is a professional skill like knife work.
learn: Build a sleep strategy for late shifts
Invest in footwear and floor mats (seriously)
Learn the stretch-and-strengthen routine kitchen veterans swear by
Decide your decade plan: kitchen, floor, or management

resources.title: BLS OOH — Food and Serving Occupations
